author: by Armen G. Kaprelian
note: Off the wire (round 10, the author's item 15): about one wire item in fifty is a cat fact from this pool, each true and light, each checked on 26 October 2026 against the reference beside it (the references are recorded in motion/README.md and never shown on screen). Atlas only, never the video.

facts.text: Cats can see with about one sixth of the light people need.
A cat hears up to about 79 kilohertz, far above the human ceiling.
facts.source: Wikipedia, Cat: senses (hearing, 55 Hz to 79 kHz)

facts.text: A cat's hearing is sharpest between 500 hertz and 32 kilohertz.
Cats sleep 12 to 16 hours a day, 13 to 14 on average.
The name Felis catus was given by Carl Linnaeus in 1758.
The domestic cat descends from the African wildcat, Felis lybica; taming began in the Near East around 7500 BCE.
facts.source: Wikipedia, Cat: domestication; Driscoll et al. 2007, Science 317: 519

facts.text: Domestic cats trace to at least five founding wildcat lineages of the Fertile Crescent.
facts.source: Driscoll et al. 2007, The Near Eastern origin of cat domestication, Science 317: 519-523

facts.text: The oldest known cat burial, at Shillourokambos on Cyprus, is about 9,500 years old; the cat lay 40 centimetres from a person.
facts.source: National Geographic, 8 April 2004 (Vigne et al. 2004, Science)

facts.text: Cats cannot taste sweetness: their sweet-receptor gene Tas1r2 is a pseudogene.
facts.source: Li et al. 2005, PLoS Genetics 1(1): e3

facts.text: A cat purrs at 25 to 150 hertz, on the in-breath and the out-breath alike.
facts.source: Scientific American, Why do cats purr? (Leslie Lyons), 2006

facts.text: The spines on a cat's tongue are scoop-shaped: they carry saliva deep into the fur, and the cat cools as it dries.
facts.source: Noel and Hu 2018, PNAS 115: 12377; National Geographic, November 2018

facts.text: A cat has five toes on each front paw and four on each hind paw: eighteen in all.
A cat's collarbones float free, held by muscle rather than joined to other bones.
Cats sweat mainly through their paw pads.
A cat's third eyelid is the nictitating membrane.
A cat moves each ear on its own.
A cat's claws rest sheathed and extend at will.
The righting reflex appears at three to four weeks of age and is perfected by six to nine.
A cat falling from up to three metres can right itself and land on its paws.
The ancient Egyptian word for cat was mjw; cats appear in Egyptian scenes from about 1980 BC.
Bastet, the Egyptian cat goddess, is attested from the Second Dynasty onward.
The Hermitage in St Petersburg keeps cats in its basements against mice, as Empress Elizabeth ordered in 1745.
The Hermitage's cats have their own press secretary and a Hermitage Cat Day every spring.
The Siberian is a centuries-old natural variety of cat from Russia and its national cat.
Siberian cats appear in Slavic folktales and artwork from the 10th century.
The Russian Blue may have begun as a landrace in the port of Arkhangelsk; the Archangel Blues have emerald-green eyes.
The Kurilian Bobtail, with a pom-pom tail of 2 to 10 vertebrae, is a natural breed of the Kuril Islands, Sakhalin and Kamchatka.
Catnip's nepetalactone delights about two thirds of cats; leopards, cougars, servals and lynxes often react too.
Cats younger than six months may not react to catnip at all.
The world's first cat café opened in Taipei in 1998; Japan's first in Osaka in 2004.
On Aoshima, Japan's Cat Island, cats have outnumbered people by up to 36 to one.
The first cat show was held at the Crystal Palace in London in 1871, organised by Harrison Weir.
The Maine Coon, one of the largest breeds, has been Maine's official state cat since 1985.
A male Maine Coon weighs 8 to 10 kilograms on average.
The longest domestic cat on record, Stewie, a Maine Coon, measured 123 centimetres from nose to tail tip in 2010.
facts.source: Guinness World Records, Stewie, the longest cat in the world (2011)

facts.text: The oldest cat on record, Creme Puff of Austin, Texas, lived 38 years and 3 days.
facts.source: Guinness World Records, Oldest cat ever

facts.text: Nearly 60 polydactyl cats live at the Hemingway Home in Key West, descended from Snow White, a six-toed cat a ship's captain gave Hemingway.
facts.source: The Ernest Hemingway Home and Museum, Our cats

facts.text: Hemingway named his cats after famous people, and the Key West museum keeps the custom.
facts.source: The Ernest Hemingway Home and Museum, Our cats

facts.text: A cat's cerebral cortex holds about 250 million neurons.
facts.source: Jardim-Messeder et al. 2017, Frontiers in Neuroanatomy 11: 118

facts.text: The orange-coat mutation sits near the Arhgap36 gene on the X chromosome; two teams found it in May 2025.
facts.source: Scientific American, May 2025 (Kaelin et al. and Sasaki et al. 2025, Current Biology)

facts.text: An adult cat's heart beats 140 to 220 times a minute; at rest it takes 20 to 30 breaths.
facts.source: Vetstreet, Feline fine: how to read your cat's vital signs (Marty Becker)

facts.text: A cat's normal temperature runs from 100 to 102.5 degrees Fahrenheit, about 37.8 to 39.2 Celsius.
facts.source: Vetstreet, Feline fine: how to read your cat's vital signs (Marty Becker)

facts.text: Whiskers grow above a cat's eyes and on its forelegs as well as on the muzzle.
The average pet cat's lifespan rose from about 7 years in the early 1980s to about 13 by 2014.
